2.3.2

Latest release27 November 2026

2.3.1 was tagged but never published; its changes ship here.

  • A Gemini chat no longer stops working after 30 minutes idle, after a gateway restart, or when a chat that began on another model switches to Gemini. By default (geminiSessions.resume: "replay") GateFox starts a new Gemini session that receives the whole chat once, instead of refusing with an error the app showed as "overloaded". That turn is as slow as a first turn. resume: "refuse" keeps the old behaviour, now with a message that says to start a new chat. Each new Gemini session records startMs, how long Antigravity took to start. See docs/gemini-sessions.md.
  • A picker row no longer repeats its account: when the model name already starts with the account label, the row shows the model alone ("Gemini 4 Neon", not "Gemini · Gemini 4 Neon"; "Qwen 3.8 Flash Next", not "Qwen · Qwen 3.8 Flash Next"). A raw model ID keeps its account ("Claude · claude-fable-5-1").

GitHub release ↗Download for Mac

2.3.0

25 November 2026
  • One local model can be served by several self-hosted machines without a separate router: a provider's pool names the machines, each of which is also its own picker row. GateFox keeps every conversation on the machine that holds its prompt cache, starts new ones where there is room, moves them away from a drained, unreachable or frozen machine, and never replays a request after output began. See docs/provider-pool.md.
  • A provider on this Mac that resets a connection at the wrong moment can no longer end the whole gateway. Node 24's fetch throws setTypeOfService EINVAL outside the request on macOS in that case; GateFox now ignores it as undici's own fix does, and the request fails with the real network error.

2.2.7

24 November 2026
  • Hovering a model in the ChatGPT or Codex app picker shows the provider's own description, such as "Fast, go-to model for coding and everyday work." for Codex models or "Fastest for quick answers" for Claude models. Gemini through Antigravity reports no descriptions, so its rows keep the route text. Existing aliases pick up descriptions at the next automatic latest-model check.
  • Phone control of a Mac works again after ChatGPT 26.1120. Its engine (0.171.0-alpha.13.2) was not on the verified list, so the native relay refused to start, paused as failing, and the phone could not reach the Mac. Its remote-control transport, processor, sign-in storage and database migrations are unchanged from 0.171.0-alpha.13, so the relay accepts it and the native host shares it after the shared-native checks.
  • gateway health --smoke no longer fails with phase unknown against ChatGPT engines from 0.171. They also send GET /models with no body, and the check's fixture provider parsed every body as JSON, so the check crashed even though every phase it had reached passed. The fixture now answers anything other than a Responses POST with 404.

2.2.6

24 November 2026
  • Managed worker routes can offer a model's full window. A route may advertise up to 1,048,576 tokens (never more than its smallest candidate allows) and accept requests up to 16 MiB, and a configuration may hold 16 routes. Until now routes stopped at 262,144 tokens, 4 MiB and 8 routes, so a Sonnet, Opus, Sol or Terra worker behind a route got less than half of its window. Existing routes and worker pins are unchanged.
  • A managed route can set selectBy: "headroom" to start each new worker on the eligible subscription account with the most quota left, instead of the first one in its list. The choice is pinned for that worker.

GitHub release ↗Download for Mac

2.2.5

24 November 2026
  • A Claude chat no longer stops with malformed_tool_call when the computer sleeps or the network drops while Claude writes a tool call. GateFox drops the unfinished call and lets Claude Code resume the reply on the same session; calls that had finished are still forwarded. An unfinished call without any input yet could previously be read as {}. If Claude Code cannot resume, the request fails with a retryable error that names the lost connection, and the chat is not held.
  • An overloaded Mac no longer breaks gateway chats as easily. Opening an existing chat uses the saved model list when the live one is slow or unreachable, instead of failing with "Gateway model discovery is unavailable"; starting a chat or turn still checks the host, with one longer try. A queued message gets 30 seconds instead of 5 before its session is closed, and a Claude process that cannot start in time is a retryable error twice before it is final.
  • A final failure from a Claude session kept across an update stays final instead of becoming a retryable provider_failed.

If the hook itself fails, agy refuses the call.

2.1.7

21 November 2026
  • A gemini-subscription provider spends a Google AI Ultra subscription through the official Gemini CLI (gemini --acp), one long-lived session per conversation, sharing the live-session machinery already used by Grok. API keys are never used: every GEMINI_*, GOOGLE_*, VERTEX* and OTEL_* variable is removed before the CLI starts, because an ambient GEMINI_API_KEY otherwise bills the API silently instead of the subscription. The CLI signs in once into a private gateway-owned home, the credential stays in that home rather than the macOS keychain, and a home that is not signed in fails with 401 before any CLI spawns. The CLI keeps no tools of its own: a gateway-written policy at the CLI's user tier denies every native tool and tells only the caller's mcp_gateway_* tools to ask (its bundled default policies otherwise run its read-only tools with no permission request), tools.exclude drops the same built-ins from its registry so the model is never offered them, and both system-scope settings paths are pinned to files that do not exist so nothing outside the home can outrank the managed settings. Any announcement of a tool the caller never offered ends the session, every permission is answered by the gateway with allow_once at most, and prompts are framed so a caller message beginning with / can never reach the CLI as one of its own commands. Sign in with gateway login gemini. See Gemini sessions.
  • Gemini sessions no longer leave transcripts behind or open a browser. Each CLI process runs in its own disposable home (the CLI records every prompt and cannot be told not to), a refreshed sign-in is copied back atomically under the home lock, and a request with no conversation id closes its session when its turn ends instead of holding a slot for thirty minutes. A saved sign-in that can no longer refresh now fails with 401 instead of opening a browser tab: the CLI's browser opener is a stand-in during inference. Reconnect and gateway login gemini answer the CLI's consent question, open the sign-in URL themselves and succeed only when the credential file appears, in an empty private working directory; a .env in the Gemini home is refused. A gateway that exits during a sign-in or a session start now kills the CLI and removes its scratch home (with the copied credential) at exit, and the next run sweeps scratch homes a killed gateway left behind.

1.9.8

12 November 2026
  • An unused phone connection no longer blocks updates. The native relay kept each remote stream's engine running until the stream closed, and while its cloud connection failed with 409 Conflict the SDK's idle sweep never closed it, so one stream on macbook-server held an old release for more than eight hours and left the rollout at process_version_pending. The relay now ends a session after 10 minutes with no traffic, no running turn and no request or approval waiting (idle_released). The phone reconnects on its next use.

  • The tailnet listener now works with the App Store build of Tailscale. That build is sandboxed and could not write the certificate to the gateway's state directory ("operation not permitted"), so the listener stayed closed. The gateway now reads the certificate and key from tailscale cert output, checks that they match, and keeps them in memory only. The copy that 1.9.6 wrote is removed.

1.9.6

12 November 2026
  • The tailnet listener serves HTTPS. Claude Desktop accepts a plain http:// gateway only on loopback, and its configuration window drops any other http:// URL when it saves, so the 1.9.3 endpoint could not be used. The gateway now serves the tailnet with this Mac's own Tailscale certificate (Let's Encrypt, from tailscale cert), fetches and renews it itself, and stays closed on the tailnet without one. gateway claude-desktop configure --direct --tailnet writes the https://NAME.ts.net:PORT endpoint. The tailnet must allow HTTPS certificates. The Mac app's Tailscale binary runs as its command line from the background service (TAILSCALE_BE_CLI=1); without it, it tried to open its GUI and the certificate was never fetched. 1.9.5 was not published.

1.8.0

9 November 2026

  • A Claude chat whose login fails before any reply, tool result or queued message no longer stays blocked behind a crash hold. The next request tries the saved login again. A failure after the turn produced output keeps the hold, because the turn may have advanced. See docs/claude-sessions.md.

  • A Claude chat whose login fails before any reply, tool result or queued message no longer stays blocked behind a crash hold. The next request tries the saved login again. A failure after the turn produced output keeps the hold, because the turn may have advanced. See docs/claude-sessions.md.

  • The app is GateFox.app, published as GateFox-VERSION-macos-arm64.zip with gatefox-VERSION-macos-arm64.tar.gz, under the standard vVERSION tag only. A Mac updated from 1.7.x first gets the new app at its old Harness Gateway.app path; at its next launch the app renames itself to GateFox.app beside it, relaunches, and moves the service and the command-line runtime to the new path. Permissions stay, because the bundle identifier and signature are unchanged. The rename waits while an update is unfinished. See docs/macos-updates.md.

  • The installer also writes a gatefox command, with the same contents as harness-gateway and gateway, which keep working. An update run by a 1.7.x app adds it at the next install, because that updater refuses receipts it does not know.

  • Fresh installations use ~/.local/share/gatefox and ~/Library/Application Support/GateFox (~/.config/gatefox on Linux). A Mac installed earlier keeps its subscription-gateway folders; nothing moves. The signed service launcher, the updater, uninstall and the app accept both.

  • The Claude Desktop profile and the ChatGPT sign-in agent are named GateFox. A profile created as Harness Gateway is still selected.

  • After a service restart, a desktop, relay session or SSH listener no longer takes the native ChatGPT engine away from the gateway host. The new host's claim could lose to the old host that was still exiting; the next client then started its own private engine, and every later client joined it, so rollout stayed native_owner_pending until every client disconnected. While no private engines hold the native home, a refused client now asks the host again for up to 20 seconds instead.

  • New gateway chats are recorded with the provider id gatefox. Chats saved earlier keep subscription_gateway, which every engine still registers and every list still shows, so nothing needs reopening. gateway desktop register publishes a native row for both ids, so ChatGPT's own engine opens either. The native-config guard refuses both ids. Executors carry GATEFOX_EXECUTOR (and the older marker). The patched SDK is gateway-executor-v4. See docs/harness-identity.md and docs/gatefox-rename.md.

  • gatefox.dev has search and sharing metadata on every page: canonical URLs, Open Graph and Twitter cards with a share image per page, JSON-LD, robots.txt, a sitemap with images and a web manifest. The deploy adds the IndexNow key file.

The long README moved to docs/cli.md, and docs/reference.html is a new searchable index of every doc, generated from each page's summary by npm run docs:site and checked by npm run check.
